#### Part A: Importing and Inspecting a CSV
##### A1
###### Import employees.csv into a data frame named emp_df using read.csv() with stringsAsFactors = FALSE.
```{r}
emp_df <- read.csv("employees.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```
##### A2
###### Display the structure, the first 5 rows, and summary of emp_df.
```{r}
str(emp_df)
head(emp_df, 5)
summary(emp_df)
```
##### A3 
###### Print the number of rows and columns of emp_df, and the class of every column
```{r}
nrow(emp_df)
ncol(emp_df)
sapply(emp_df, class)
```
##### A4 
###### Print the mean salary, the maximum age, and the number of employees in each department
```{r}
mean(emp_df$salary, na.rm = TRUE)
max(emp_df$age, na.rm = TRUE)
table(emp_df$department)
```
#### Part B: Creating Data Frames
##### B1 
###### Create a data frame new_hires with the same column names as emp_df and the three new employees
```{r}
new_hires <- data.frame(
  emp_id = c(21, 22, 23),
  name = c("Uma", "Victor", "Wen"),
  department = c("HR", "IT", "Sales"),
  sex = c("F", "M", "F"),
  age = c(28, 37, 33),
  salary = c(45000, 83000, 60000),
  years_service = c(2, 9, 6),
  rating = c(3, 4, 5)
)
```
##### B2
###### Use rbind() to append new_hires to emp_df, saving the result as emp_all and print dimensions
```{r}
emp_all <- rbind(emp_df, new_hires)
dim(emp_all)
```
##### B3
###### Add a column bonus to emp_all equal to 5% of salary, rounded to the nearest whole number
```{r}
emp_all$bonus <- round(emp_all$salary * 0.05)
```
Part C: Subsetting
##### C1 
###### Extract the first 5 rows and only the columns name and salary
```{r}
emp_all[1:5, c("name", "salary")]
```
##### C2 
###### Using logical subsetting, select all employees with salary greater than 70000
```{r}
emp_all[emp_all$salary > 70000, ]
```
##### C3 
###### Select employees in the "IT" department with years_service of at least 5 returning name, years_service, and salary
```{r}
subset(emp_all, department == "IT" & years_service >= 5, select = c(name, years_service, salary))
```
##### C4 
###### Use which() to print the row numbers of employees older than 50, then print their names
```{r}
older_rows <- which(emp_all$age > 50)
print(older_rows)
print(emp_all$name[older_rows])
```
##### C5 
###### Remove the columns emp_id and bonus using negative indexing; print the first 3 rows of the result
```{r}
head(emp_all[, !names(emp_all) %in% c("emp_id", "bonus")], 3)
```
##### C6 
###### Using logical indexing, print the salary of the employee whose name is "Mia"
```{r}
emp_all$salary[emp_all$name == "Mia"]
```
#### Part D: Factors
##### D1 
###### Convert department and sex in emp_all to factors with factor(). Print levels() of each.
```{r}
emp_all$department <- factor(emp_all$department)
emp_all$sex <- factor(emp_all$sex)
levels(emp_all$department)
levels(emp_all$sex)
```
##### D2 
###### Use table() to count employees per department, and make a two-way table of department by sex
```{r}
table(emp_all$department)
table(emp_all$department, emp_all$sex)
```
##### D3 
###### Create an ordered factor rating_level from rating using factor() with levels 1:5 and labels
```{r}
emp_all$rating_level <- factor(emp_all$rating, levels = 1:5, labels = c("Poor", "Fair", "Good", "Very Good", "Excellent"), ordered = TRUE)
table(emp_all$rating_level)
```
##### D4 
###### Using a for loop over levels(emp_all$department) and logical subsetting, print mean salary rounded to nearest whole number
```{r}
for (dept in levels(emp_all$department)) {
  mean_sal <- mean(emp_all$salary[emp_all$department == dept], na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(dept, ":", round(mean_sal), "\n")
}
```
#### Part E: Conditional Statements
##### E1 
###### Using nested ifelse(), add a column salary_band: "High" (>=70k), "Medium" (50k-70k), else "Low"
```{r}
emp_all$salary_band <- ifelse(emp_all$salary >= 70000, "High",
                              ifelse(emp_all$salary >= 50000, "Medium", "Low"))
table(emp_all$salary_band)
```
##### E2 
###### Using ifelse(), add a column level: "Senior" if years_service >= 8, otherwise "Junior"
```{r}
emp_all$level <- ifelse(emp_all$years_service >= 8, "Senior", "Junior")
table(emp_all$level)
```
##### E3 
###### Write a function raise_pct(rating) using if/else if/else chain (0.10 for 5, 0.07 for 4, 0.04 for 3, 0 otherwise)
```{r}
raise_pct <- function(rating) {
  if (rating == 5) {
    return(0.10)
  } else if (rating == 4) {
    return(0.07)
  } else if (rating == 3) {
    return(0.04)
  } else {
    return(0)
  }
}
emp_all$raise <- sapply(emp_all$rating, raise_pct)
emp_all$new_salary <- round(emp_all$salary * (1 + emp_all$raise))
head(emp_all[, c("name", "rating", "raise", "new_salary")], 5)
```
##### E4 
###### Using an if/else statement, compute total new salary and check against 1,600,000 threshold
```{r}
total_budget <- sum(emp_all$new_salary)
if (total_budget < 1600000) {
  print("Budget OK")
} else {
  print("Over budget")
}
print(total_budget)
```
#### Part F: Sorting
##### F1 
###### Use sort() to print the 5 highest salary values in decreasing order, and first 5 employee names alphabetically
```{r}
head(sort(emp_all$salary, decreasing = TRUE), 5)
head(sort(emp_all$name), 5)
```
##### F2 
###### Use order() to sort emp_all by salary in descending order and print name, department, salary of top 5
```{r}
sorted_indices <- order(emp_all$salary, decreasing = TRUE)
by_salary <- emp_all[sorted_indices, c("name", "department", "salary")]
head(by_salary, 5)
```
